correctness.rationale: The upper bound follows from the \(n\) principal opens \(X\cup\{d_i\}\), each with a maximum, together with the finite-space category bound. For the lower bound, fewer than \(n^2\) open motion-planning domains force one lower set to contain two distinct maximal pairs. If their second coordinates differ, slicing at any \(x\in X\) makes the inclusion of \(X\oplus\{b,d\}\) null-homotopic; the explicit order retraction from \(X\oplus D_n\) onto that two-top subspace would then make its identity null-homotopic. The first-coordinate case is symmetric. Kandola's non-Hausdorff-suspension result supplies the required noncontractibility obstruction. The proof is symbolic and the finite checker is not used as an infinite proof.
